title: Stage-gate CI operator and automated dependency upgrade workflows
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Our CI matrix has become brittle and noisy when dependency upgrades and gated promotion flows run in the same pipelines. This PR introduces a lightweight stage-gate operator in the CI control plane and extracts dependency-upgrade automation into a dedicated workflow that runs policy checks and can open candidate upgrade PRs. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy rebuilds for unrelated CI stages; 2) Make dependabot-style upgrades safer by gating them with quick infra/e2e smoke and policy checks; 3) Reduce time-to-merge for low-risk changes by letting non-blocking stages run post-merge. What this changes (summary): - A stage-gate operator (ci/tools/stage_gate_operator) implemented as a small Go binary + Dockerfile that coordinates stage transitions using commit metadata and a new GitHub Actions composite action. - New workflow .github/workflows/ci-stage-gate.yml that orchestrates lint/unit -> optional integration -> deploy-stage gates and exposes an API for other workflows to call into the operator. - Automated dep upgrade workflow .github/workflows/auto-dep-upgrades.yml that runs nightly, performs policy checks (license, semver-compatibility heuristics), runs fast smoke tests, and opens upgrade PRs against feature/dep-upgrades/* when safe. - Small refactors to existing composite actions to accept a "gated" flag and emit gate events. - Docs: docs/ci/stage-gates.md and a short runbook for on-call. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-7842 - [x] Stage-gate operator unit tests - [x] Smoke CI job added and kept intentionally small (30s median) - [x] Upgrade workflow dry-run tested against staging repo - [x] Docs and runbook added - [x] Manual rollout: enabled for redwood/ and redwood-docs/ first Implementation notes: The operator intentionally keeps state out of the repo and writes transient state to the Actions artifact store to avoid introducing a new DB. Gate transitions are signed with the runner identity and recorded in the PR timeline for auditability. The dependency upgrade workflow runs in a constrained container with pinned tool versions to limit flakiness. Rollout plan: 1) enable operator in a canary subset of repos (redwood, redwood-docs) 2) monitor gate-outcome metrics and false-positive rate for 2 weeks 3) expand to other repositories. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior of CI remains unchanged for branches that do not opt into stage gates. Related: ENG-7901 (policy checks for upgrades).

review_conversation: Ethan Zhao (2026-02-19): Nice separation of concerns. Question about using Actions artifact store for transient state—any retention implications?
Maya Patel (2026-02-19): We set retention to 7 days for gate artifacts; runbook explains emergency TTL extension. Keeping no long-term state avoids DB ops for rollout.
Renee Alvarez (2026-02-22): CI timings look good but one flaky test in smoke needs a flake guard. Suggest adding --max-retries=2 to the smoke script.
Maya Patel (2026-02-23): Added retry guard and a comments in the test harness. PTAL.
